drafted_from: tool row in tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/tool-rows.json, do-work/build_training_rows.py and test/test_fine_tune.py (BuildRows), which I ran on its made-up fixture
start_here: Say to your AI: "Build the training rows for my two writing rules plain-words and said-aloud from my ruled lines, holding the test lines out first, into /work/out." It reads your settings row and your rules, writes a request file and runs build_training_rows.py on your computer.
instructions: 1. Pour the two example rows into your own settings list (see pour), or make list:settings from them, then put your own seed, test share, set names and numbers in the build, train and score objects: every law, line, set name and number is yours, none is built in.

2. Collect your laws ({law id: question, options (two answers), fail (the answer that fails a line), bad_from}) and the lines you ruled on ({text, sets, bad_for}) from your own lists; the AI reads your settings row with tool:read-a-tool-setting and passes it as settings_record.
3. The AI writes the request to a file and runs python3 -I tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/do-work/build_training_rows.py <request file>; the same request always makes the same rows.

4. Read the summary lines and the last line {"result": {items_file, train_file, items, train_items, test_items, train_rows, synthetic_rows, synthetic_dropped, per_law}}. A law with only a handful of bad test lines cannot be measured: say so. Then train with tool:train-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules.

worked_examples.title: Build rows for two rules from four ruled lines, a transcript and captions
worked_examples.ask: Build the training rows for my two writing rules plain-words and said-aloud, holding the test lines out first.
worked_examples.given: From tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/test/test_fine_tune.py (BuildRows.test_builds_items_and_rows), which I ran. Request: laws plain-words ("Does this line use a word a child would not know?", options no and yes, fail yes) and said-aloud ("Would a person say this line out loud?", fail no); four ruled lines ("We leverage synergies." bad for plain-words, "We fix the sink." good, "Herewith the parcel." bad for stiff, "A line ruled nothing."); a talk transcript of 12 sentences, six videos of captions, seven made-up lines, one held-out card, seed 7, test_share 0.5, never_train ["Herewith the parcel."]. Command: python3 -I tools/fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules/do-work/build_training_rows.py /work/request.json.
worked_examples.hands_back: Summary lines "items 13: train 6, test 7; train rows 15 (5 synthetic); synthetic dropped as test overlap 1", "  plain-words              train bad   2 good   6 | test bad   0 good   7" and "  said-aloud               train bad   2 good   5 | test bad   0 good   7", then {"result": {"items_file": "/work/out/items.json", "train_file": "/work/out/train.jsonl", "items": 13, "train_items": 6, "test_items": 7, "train_rows": 15, "synthetic_rows": 5, "synthetic_dropped": 1, "per_law": {"plain-words": {"train_bad": 2, "train_good": 6, "test_bad": 0, "test_good": 7}, "said-aloud": {"train_bad": 2, "train_good": 5, "test_bad": 0, "test_good": 7}}}}. "Herewith the parcel." and the held-out card are in no training row; the first train row is {law plain-words, text "I walked to shop number 3 today.", gold 0, bad false, source real}. Both laws have 0 bad test lines here, so neither is measurable yet.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For the fine-tune tools the row id is record:setting:fine-tune-a-small-model-on-a-persons-rules~<scope_kind>~<scope_id> and its settings hold a build, a train and a score object that fill every request key the request leaves out.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
